title: Series and DataFrames
summary: The two pandas types: building a DataFrame, columns as Series, shape and dtypes, the index, and .loc versus .iloc.
hints: `make_people`: `pd.DataFrame({"name": [...], "age": [...], "city": [...]})`: a dict of column name to list of values, all lists the same length. `ages`: `df["age"]` is a Series named `age`.

`shape_info`: `rows, cols = df.shape`, and `list(df.columns)` for the names. `first_and_last`: `.iloc` selects by *position*, and a list selects several rows: `df.iloc[[0, -1]]`. The index labels of those rows are kept.

`by_name`: `df.set_index("name")` returns a new frame indexed by name. `row_for`: `.loc` selects by *label*, so `by_name(df).loc[name]` is one row as a Series; `.to_dict()` turns it into a plain dict. `average_age`: `float(df["age"].mean())`.
